explain.say: A click pen uses the same button press to push the tip out and pull it back in. The trick is a small part called the rotating cam, which turns a little with every click.

faq.q: What happens when you press a click pen?
faq.a: The button pushes a plunger down onto the rotating cam. Sloped teeth push the cam down past the barrel's ridges and twist it round a little.
asks: How does a clicky pen work?

faq.a: The rotating cam is a small part with ribs and sloped teeth that turns by one step on every click. Its position decides whether the tip is held out or let back in.
asks: What is inside a retractable pen?

faq.q: How does a click pen stay out?
faq.a: After one click, the cam's ribs rest on short ledges inside the barrel, which stop the spring pushing the ink tube back up.
asks: What holds the pen tip out?

faq.q: Why does a click pen need a spring?
faq.a: The spring around the ink tube always pushes the tube back up. When the cam's ribs reach the deep slots, the spring pushes the tip back inside.
asks: What pulls the tip back in?

faq.q: Why do clicky pens wear out?
faq.a: The plastic teeth and ledges rub on every click. After thousands of clicks they can wear round, and the cam may stop catching on the ledges.
asks: Why does my click pen not stay out?

facts: A click pen's cam turns one step per click, alternating between ledges and slots.
The same push-push idea is used in some cupboard latches and card slots.
